content:
Fixed with a one-character change: the base-case guard was `lo >= hi`, which returned `nil` before checking the element at `lo == hi` (so single-element tuples and every last-candidate lookup failed); it's now `lo > hi`, letting the general clause probe `mid` when the range narrows to one index.

Verified by brute force over all sorted tuples of size 0–40 (with duplicates) against every target in -55..55 — 0 mismatches — and ~16 `elem/2` probes for n=100 000 (log₂ n ≈ 16.6), so the O(log n) requirement holds.

Summary: changed the `search/4` base-case guard from `lo >= hi` to `lo > hi` so the final remaining candidate is actually compared, restoring correct results without touching the name, API, or complexity.
